correctness.rationale: The exact cell rescaling gives \(I[u_n]=n\sum_{j<n}c_j\). The first cell is computed exactly as \(8/105\). Concavity plus a standard interpolation remainder gives an absolutely summable \(O(j^{-6})\) tail, and a uniform Taylor expansion sharpens it to \(c_j=\frac{1}{196830}j^{-6}+O(j^{-7})\), which implies \(I[u_n]=Cn-\frac{1}{984150}n^{-4}+O(n^{-5})\). The packaged checker re-evaluates the exact polynomial cell integrals and asymptotic constants.
risks: The decimal value of \(C\) is numerical; the theorem itself defines \(C\) by an absolutely convergent positive series.
The finite checker does not certify the infinite asymptotic; that part rests on the analytic interpolation bound and uniform Taylor expansion reproduced in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The qualitative divergence of regular approximants and the isolated first-cell value \(8/(105h)\) are prior-covered. The accepted original claim is the exact full uniform-nodal-interpolant decomposition and sharp asymptotic with the convergent coefficient series and tail. Pereira–Cruz–Torres publish rounded values for precisely the polygonal curve through optimal nodal values but do not derive this law; Ball–Knowles and Ball's 2001 survey establish broader failure and the boundary-layer calculation without summing the full nodal interpolant; the other inspected same-object literature proposes remedies without this quantitative asymptotic.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, lecture note, or older finite-element calculation may contain the same exact nodal-interpolant asymptotic under different notation.
The published PLFOpt table numerically makes the linear rate visible, although it does not state or prove the infinite-mesh asymptotic.
The known boundary-layer constant makes the leading coefficient numerically very close to \(8/105\); an unindexed source may have carried the calculation through the remaining uniform nodal cells.

value.rationale: The uniform nodal interpolant of the known exact singular minimizer is a canonical approximation, not an arbitrary slice. The full exact linear blow-up law quantifies a standard numerical pathology and explains the published PLFOpt data beyond the already known first-cell lower bound. It identifies the precise contribution of all later cells and the sharp finite-mesh tail, giving a reproducible benchmark for exact integration and for methods designed to overcome the Lavrentiev gap.
risks: The result is a sharp benchmark for one canonical mesh family rather than a general theorem for arbitrary finite-element spaces.
The isolated first-cell obstruction is already known; value comes from completing the exact full-mesh asymptotic and explaining the published nodal data.
